articles.title: Ole Miss RB Kewan Lacy will be game-time decision for No. 4 Rebels in showdown with No. 21 Florida
articles.summary: Lacy suffered an apparent shoulder injury during the Rebels' win over LSU, but head coach Pete Golding said it "wasn't nearly as bad" as originally believed.
articles.body:
Ole Miss running back Kewan Lacy will be a game-time decision for the No. 4 Rebels as they visit No. 21 Florida on Saturday in another SEC matchup between top-25 teams.

Head coach Pete Golding announced Lacy's status during his Monday press conference, telling reporters ( via the Mississippi Clarion Ledger ) the injury "wasn't nearly as bad as we thought it was."

Lacey rushed for 43 yards on nine carries in Ole Miss' 32-24 win over No. 10 LSU before leaving the game in the third quarter with what appeared to be a left shoulder injury and was announced as "an upper-body injury."

Following the Rebels' victory, Golding told reporters that X-rays on Lacy's shoulder came back negative . The running back wanted to return to the game and play through the pain he was experiencing, but coaches decided to keep him on the sideline as a precautionary measure.

For the season, Lacy has rushed for 191 yards and four touchdowns on 39 carries. Last year, he had a breakout season with 1,567 rushing yards and 24 TDS on 306 carries, adding 177 yards on 29 receptions.

In Lacy's absence, freshman JT Lindsey rushed for 20 yards on four carries. The transfer from LSU will start against Florida if Lacy is unable to play. In three games, he's tallied 48 yards on 12 rushes.

Florida coach Jon Sumrall surprised Gators are a favorite over Ole Miss

Last season, Ole Miss defeated Florida 34-24 with Lacy rushing for 224 yards and three TDs on 31 carries. That performance may be why his potential absence has sportsbooks making the Gators the surprise favorites early in the week.

Despite the big win over LSU and their higher ranking in the AP Top 25 poll, the Rebels are 3.5-point underdogs to the Gators ahead of their matchup.

Informed of that by a reporter at his Monday press conference, Florida head coach Jon Sumrall quipped, " There's a lot of good drugs out there, huh? "

articles.title: Ole Miss football made a leap, but LSU wasn't their 'Super Bowl'
articles.summary: Pete Golding and the Rebels have a tough schedule ahead.
articles.body:
With all the drama surrounding the LSU Tigers football program leading up to last Saturday's game with the Ole Miss Rebels , Lane Kiffin's highly anticipated return to Oxford didn't go as planned.

Kiffin finally faced off against his old squad, but the reunion was spoiled in exciting fashion. Ole Miss showed their old coach he made a mistake by leaving the Rebels right before the team's College Football Playoff run last season.

The Rebels started the game jumping out to an early 24-7 lead at halftime. However, the second half was a different story. The Tigers came roaring back and tied the game at 24 in the fourth quarter. This was the moment that Ole Miss showed the nation who they were.

While being outscored 17-0 before the game-winning touchdown, Rebels quarterback Trinidad Chambliss and the offense drove 75 yards down the field to score and successfully converted a two-point conversion to go up by eight points and end the LSU run.

Kiffin gave credit to Chambliss for the victory, labeling him "the hardest player to play in America." He gave credit to the monster he created and even took credit for the stadium being full an hour before kickoff.

Ole Miss coach Pete Golding said after the game, "It wasn't the Super Bowl, and we didn't make it to be the Super Bowl."

The Rebels showed just how dominant they can be in a big prime-time game. This was an early glimpse of what the Playoff atmosphere would be like in Oxford with a return run. Needless to say, the Rebels stepped up to the plate, again.

Under Golding, the Rebels won two Playoff games, but that was with Kiffin's roster. Now he could start his own dynasty and do something even greater. Bringing a national championship to Oxford for the first time in 66 years is the ultimate goal.

Golding's comment about the game not being their Super Bowl was precise because of their fierce competition with the rest of the schedule. He knows LSU was the first of many major tests this season.

They still face a revamped No. 21 Florida team next week in the swamp, No. 1 Texas Longhorns in Austin, and No. 4 Georgia at home. The rest of the season will not be any easier for the Rebels.

With Kiffin no longer around calling the shots, beating LSU will either prove to be a stepping stone or a fluke. We'll wait to see what Ole Miss is made of down the stretch.

articles.title: Vote for The Daily Herald's TSSAA football athlete of the Week from Week 5
articles.summary: Vote here to decide The Daily Herald's Columbia area TSSAA football Athlete of the Week from Week 5 of the high school season.
articles.body:
We're through another Friday night in the Tennessee high school football season and there was no shortage of standout performers across the Columbia area in Week 5 .

Now you can cast your vote to decide The Daily Herald's TSSAA football Athlete of the Week.

Nathanel Karkau, Columbia Academy: Karkau caught three passes for 44 yards and a score, and on defense had five tackles and a sack.

Daniel Booker, Columbia Central: Booker completed 12-of-16 passes for 172 yards and three touchdowns, while also rushing six times for 75 yards and two touchdowns in a 45-7 win over Lawrence County.

Brody Bullock, Independence: Bullock caught six passes for 114 yards and two touchdowns, while also rushing for a touchdown, in a 56-14 win over Coffee County. On defense he added an interception returned for 27 yards.

Caden Hagan, Loretto: Hagan had 15 carries for 166 yards and three touchdowns in a 35-28 defeat to Collinwood.

Jonah Gipson, Spring Hill: Gipson rushed 12 times for 101 yards and two touchdowns while also completing 6-of-10 passes for 45 yards in a 36-12 win over Maplewood.

McKaleb Powell, Summertown: Powell had 114 all-purpose yards and two total touchdowns in a 30-7 win over Scotts Hill.

Micah Sally, Summit: Sally caught 10 passes for 125 yards and two touchdowns in a 42-21 defeat to Lincoln County.

Cam Surratt, Zion Christian: Surratt was 15-for-21 passing with 270 yards, two touchdowns and an interception in a 43-12 defeat to Christian Community.

Be sure to cast your vote below before the poll closes at noon on Thursday.
